findings.evidence: Artin.lean:207-212 proves `hP` via `isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Nat.card_pos.ne')`, i.e. CharZero is consumed only for subgroup-order invertibility; `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indCharacterSpanInt` (Spanning.lean:378-382) asks only `∀ C, P C → IsUnit (Nat.card C : k)`; `TauCeti.isUnit_natCard_subgroup` (TauCeti/GroupTheory/Index.lean:169) turns `IsUnit (Nat.card G : k)` into that hypothesis for every subgroup.
findings.fix: State it as `theorem natCard_nsmul_mem_indCharacterSpanInt_isCyclic [IsAlgClosed k] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)]`, discharging the comparison hypothesis with `fun C _ ↦ isUnit_natCard_subgroup C (isUnit_of_invertible _)` (the exact idiom the PR deletes from Artin.lean). If you want the fully hypothesis-free-in-characteristic form, `[IsAlgClosed k]` alone also suffices by case-splitting on `(Nat.card G : k) = 0`, where the left side is `0` and membership is trivial — the file already documents that convention for the canonical theorems.
findings.issue: `natCard_nsmul_mem_indCharacterSpanInt_isCyclic` assumes `[CharZero k]`, which is strictly stronger than what the proof uses and than the convention of the rest of the directory: it is the only `CharZero` in `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/`, while `indCharacterSpan_cyclic_eq_top` (Spanning.lean:439), `indCharacterSpan_eq_top` (Spanning.lean:423) and the deleted `indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpanCyclic` all use `[Invertible (Nat.card G : k)]`. CharZero is used only to discharge `IsUnit (Nat.card C : k)` for cyclic `C`, excluding the standard non-modular case char k = p ∤ |G|.

findings.evidence: Ideal.lean:258-259 `have hf : n • (f : G → k) ∈ … := by simpa [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters f.2 h` versus Artin.lean:200-202 `simpa [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters hf (natCard_nsmul_one_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic …)`.
findings.fix: Add the general lemma in Ideal.lean next to `mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters`, e.g. `theorem nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_of_nsmul_one_mem {n : ℕ} (h : n • (1 : G → k) ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P) {f : G → k} (hf : f ∈ virtualCharacters k G) : n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`, and use it in both places; the cyclic and elementary theorems then become instantiations.
findings.issue: The family-general step "`n • 1 ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P` and `f ∈ virtualCharacters k G` imply `n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`" is never stated; the identical `simpa [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters …` proof appears twice, once inside `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective_of_nsmul_one_mem` (Ideal.lean:258-259) and once as the cyclic special case `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` (Artin.lean:201-202).

summary: The sharp Artin results and the rational-surjectivity criterion sit at the natural level, but the induced-character-span endpoint carries `[CharZero k]` where the nearby general comparison needs only invertibility of the subgroup orders, and the "n • 1 ⇒ n • f" step is duplicated instead of stated once family-generally.
